relationship_type: manufacturing candidate before later JEN takeover
evidence_summary: Fuzzboxes identifies early V828 production by EME followed by JEN; VoxSupreme/Lefty sources place EKO/EME in the Italian Vox production network, but the exact boundary between EKO/Recanati work and EME-branded production needs model-specific primary documentation.

Vox Showroom states wah/Crybaby production moved from early US production to EME in Recanati, then moved from EME to JEN by mid-1969; retained as an explicit period manufacturing switch rather than generic JEN attribution.
Fuzzboxes and Vox Showroom identify later Italian V828 production as JEN-built; model is kept separate from its earlier EME production state.

Multiple independent database records and Vox-family evidence support JEN's own-branded fuzz products as part of the same Italian production ecosystem used for Vox and OEM labels; individual models remain separately cataloged.
Effects Database identifies Elka Fuzz as built in Italy by Jen Pescara and places it in the same design family as Jen/Unicord/Luxor/Nova examples; treated as an OEM identity, not a separate factory.
Effects Database and cross-family evidence place Luxor Fuzz in the Jen-built Italian OEM family; marketed label remains distinct.
Effects Database identifies Nova Tone Bender as part of the Jen-built Italian family; retained as a separate marketed identity.
Effects Database identifies the Unicord Fuzz as built in Italy by Jen Pescara and distinguishes Unicord as the marketed identity; no physical-builder merge into Unicord is made.

VoxSupreme and Lefty document EKO's Recanati production role and the emergence of EME in the same Italian manufacturing network, but this is not enough to assign every Vox-branded pedal directly to EKO; use only as context until model-level evidence exists.
